messages:
alyssa: heads up, hitting 401s when switching my mac env to use .env file for the SDK auth. works if I paste the header directly in curl though :confused:

matt: can you paste the header you generated and the curl that works? also which shell (zsh/bash) and how are you setting the env?

alyssa: sure — using zsh, dotenv loaded by Direnv. curl that works: ```curl -H "Authorization: Basic QWxhZGRpbjpPcGVuU2VzYW1l" https://api.redwood-inference.dev/v1/..```

alyssa: but in node process.env.REDWOOD_KEY I have the raw key and Buffer.from(process.env.REDWOOD_KEY).toString('base64') gives a different string and server rejects it

samir: common gotcha: basic auth needs base64(api_key + ':') — note the trailing colon even if password is empty. if you only base64(api_key) that won't match.

jordana: also check for stray quotes/newlines from dotenv or copy/paste. e.g. if REDWOOD_KEY="sk-abc..." the quotes become part of the key. on mac pbcopy sometimes copies a trailing newline depending how you pipe it.

kevin: echo adds newline by default. if you do `echo $KEY | pbcopy` you'll include a newline. use `echo -n $KEY | pbcopy` or `printf '%s' "$KEY" | pbcopy` so base64 matches.

alyssa: ohhh that explains a lot — I was copying from a text file with CRLF and probably had an extra char. quick q: what's the canonical way to produce the Authorization header in different languages?

samir: quick cheatsheet:
- curl: `-H "Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s:' "$KEY" | base64)"` (note the colon inside printf)
- node (server): ```const basic = Buffer.from(`${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}:`).toString('base64'); headers['Authorization'] = `Basic ${basic}`;```
- python requests: either `requests.get(url, auth=(API_KEY, ''))` or manually: ```import base64
h = base64.b64encode((API_KEY + ':').encode()).decode()
headers={'Authorization': f'Basic {h}'} ```
- go net/http: ```req.SetBasicAuth(API_KEY, "")``` (this handles the colon for you)

jordana: +1 on SetBasicAuth — it percent-escapes and handles header formatting. also be careful with libraries that accept an auth token directly vs basic auth; some SDKs expect `Bearer` tokens and will double-wrap if you plug a basic header in incorrectly.

matt: another subtle one: some base64 implementations insert newlines for long inputs (very rare for api keys), `base64 --wrap=0` avoids that. on mac BSD base64 you can do `base64` which doesn't wrap by default, on linux GNU base64 has `-w` option.

alyssa: thanks — I changed my dotenv to no quotes, updated my direnv to trim, and using Buffer.from(`${KEY}:`).toString('base64') fixed it. tests pass now. :tada:

deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch fix/auth-dotenv at 1805001300 — will run smoke tests after deploy.

kevin: fwiw, for developer DX we should add a short note in the SDK auth docs about the trailing colon and common env quoting issues. I can add a small snippet and example commands.

jordana: please do — maybe add a tiny troubleshooting section: quotes in .env, pbcopy/echo newlines, SetBasicAuth note, and curl one-liner. would save 3 pings a week :grin:

alyssa: adding a quick PR now with the exact snippets I used. ping me for review if you want the Mac/Linux variants.

samir: nice! thanks for tracking this down.
